battle.name: 第二次世界大戰
battle.theater: 歐非亞三洲與太平洋戰場
battle.brief: 1939年9月1日德軍進攻波蘭，戰火六年橫掃歐非亞三洲與太平洋，1945年9月2日以日本在東京灣簽署降書作結。卡面那門1850年德國嘴射野戰砲早已退場，但它開出的線膛加鋼製後膛路線，一路演成德軍七七公分野戰砲與美軍一零五公分榴彈砲，決定了各戰線的射程與火力節奏。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries:
交戰方在歐洲、非洲、亞洲與太平洋同時運作，但實際上分成幾套各自獨立的指揮體系。軸心國一邊的核心是德國、義大利與日本：德國以國防軍最高統帥部統轄陸軍、海軍與空軍，一九三八年起由威廉·凱特爾元帥任武裝力量最高統帥，弗朗茨·哈爾德任陸軍參謀總長；義大利以最高統帥部統編，維托里奧·墨索里尼任最高統帥兼陸軍元帥，具體作戰多由陸軍參謀總部承擔；日本以大本營與陸軍參謀本部運作，一九三六年後由裕仁天皇在御前會議裁決，軍令與政令合一。軸心陣營還包括匈牙利、羅馬尼亞、保加利亞、芬蘭、斯洛伐克、克羅地亞等國，以及數個佔領區政權。
同盟國一邊同樣不是單一指揮部：英國以帝國參謀總部為核心，邱吉爾自一九四〇年五月起兼任首相與國防大臣，國協海陸空軍在印度、中東與東非分別作戰；法國淪陷後戴高樂於一九四〇年六月成立自由法國，與英軍並肩在北非、義大利與西北歐作戰；蘇聯在一九四一年六月二十二日巴巴羅莎行動後才以大本營介入，最高統帥先後由鐵木辛哥與朱可夫接掌；美國在一九四一年十二月八日珍珠港事變後加入，先由參謀總部主導作戰，一九四二年起設歐洲戰區盟軍最高統帥部，由艾森豪威爾統率。中國自一九三七年全面抗戰起即為同盟國作戰，蔣介石任中國戰區最高統帥，英美第十四航空隊等聯合單位亦在華運作。總體而言，一九四二年起由同盟國參謀總部以英美參謀長會議協調大西洋兩岸、蘇聯、中國與太平洋幾條戰線，但戰區之間的火力、兵員與情報調配，往往要拖上數月才落實。
countriesEn:
The belligerents of the Second World War operated simultaneously in Europe, Africa, Asia and the Pacific, yet they did not act from a single command. On the Axis side the core was Germany, Italy and Japan. Germany ran the war through the Oberkommando der Wehrmacht, which supervised the army, navy and air force; from 1938 Field Marshal Wilhelm Keitel served as commander-in-chief of the armed forces, with Colonel General Franz Halder as chief of the army general staff. Italy worked through its Comando Supremo, with Benito Mussolini as supreme commander and marshal of the army, while the army general staff carried out most operational planning. Japan operated through the Imperial General Headquarters and the Army General Staff, and from 1936 decisions were taken by the Emperor in imperial conferences that fused command with government. The Axis bloc also included Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Finland, Slovakia and Croatia, together with a number of regimes installed in occupied territory.
The Allied side was no more unified. Britain was organised around the Imperial General Staff, with Winston Churchill serving as prime minister and minister of defence from May 1940, and the Commonwealth services running their own campaigns in India, the Middle East and East Africa. After the collapse of France, Charles de Gaulle formed Free France in June 1940 and fought beside the British in North Africa, Italy and north-west Europe. The Soviet Union entered only after Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941, working through the Stavka, the high command, first under Semyon Timoshenko and later under Georgy Zhukov. The United States joined after the attack on Pearl Harbor on 8 December 1941, initially fighting under the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and from 1942 through the Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force under Dwight Eisenhower. China had been fighting Japan since 1937 and fought as an Allied power under Chiang Kai-shek as supreme commander of the Chinese theatre, with joint units such as the Fourteenth Air Force operating in China as well. In overall terms, from 1942 the Combined Chiefs of Staff coordinated the Atlantic, Soviet, Chinese and Pacific fronts, but the movement of artillery, troops and intelligence between distant theatres often took months to arrange.
people:
關鍵人物橫跨兩邊，也橫跨前線與後方。軸心方面，阿道夫·希特勒自一九三三年出任德國總理後把黨政軍權集中於一身，一九三九年三月擴編德國陸軍為兩百萬人並下令執行白色方案；凱特爾元帥任武裝力量最高統帥，哈爾德主持作戰計畫，倫德施泰特負責西線初期，隆美爾在北非與諾曼第與英美對峙，曼斯坦因策劃反攻與匈牙利戰役，黨衛軍裝甲師指揮官迪特里希在阿登突出部獨力支撐。義大利的墨索里尼在法國崩潰後被連勝刺激，一九四〇年六月向英法宣戰。日本方面，裕仁天皇在御前會議承擔最高決策，東條英機任首相兼陸軍大臣，近衛文麿在一九三六、一九三七年推動戰爭擴張，岡村寧次與杉山元掌參謀本部，山本五十六在珍珠港與中途島指揮聯合艦隊。
同盟國方面，邱吉爾在一九四〇年六月十八日於下議院演說表明全國將繼續抵抗，並自任戰時首相；艾森豪威爾自一九四二年八月任北非盟軍最高統帥，策劃登陸北非與霸王行動；蒙哥馬利接掌第二十一集團軍群，在阿拉曼與諾曼第指揮地面主力。蘇聯的史達林自一九四一年七月任國防委員會主席，鐵木辛哥主持巴巴羅莎防禦，朱可夫自一九四二年起接掌最高統帥部，主導斯大林格勒反攻、庫爾斯克與柏林攻勢，羅科索夫斯基與瓦丘津分統北方面軍與加里寧方面軍。中國方面，蔣介石任最高統帥，李宗仁指揮台兒莊戰役，薛岳指揮第三次長沙會戰，張自忠於一九四〇年五月殉國，彭德懷於一九四〇年八月發起百團大戰。科技與情報端同樣關鍵：英國的沃森·瓦特在一九三五年提出以脈衝波雷達偵測飛機，蒂澤德使團把成果帶到美國；布萊切利園的圖靈團隊破譯德軍密碼，破解結果在霸王行動前直接影響盟軍部署；美國海軍破譯日本海軍主力艦密碼，導致中途島海戰的先手攻擊。
peopleEn:
The decisive figures stretched across both sides and across front line and home front. On the Axis, Adolf Hitler had concentrated party, state and military power in his own hands since becoming chancellor in 1933, expanded the German army to two million men in March 1939 and ordered the implementation of Fall Weiss, the plan for the attack on Poland. Field Marshal Keitel was commander-in-chief of the armed forces and Halder ran operational planning, with Rundstedt responsible for the opening of the western front, Rommel facing the British and Americans in North Africa and Normandy, Manstein planning the counter-stroke and the Hungarian campaign, and SS tank commander Dietrich left holding the Ardennes salient on his own. Mussolini in Italy, goaded by the collapse of France, declared war on Britain and France in June 1940. In Japan the Emperor Hirohito bore the highest decisions in the imperial conferences, Tojo Hideki served as prime minister and army minister, Konoe Fumimaro drove the expansion of 1936 and 1937, Okamura Yasuji and Sugiyama Gen served at the Army General Staff, and Isoroku Yamamoto commanded the Combined Fleet at Pearl Harbor and Midway.
On the Allied side, Churchill's speech to the House of Commons on 18 June 1940 committed the country to fight on, and he remained wartime prime minister; Eisenhower took command of the Allied forces in North Africa from August 1942 and planned the landings in North Africa and Operation Overlord; Montgomery assumed the 21st Army Group and commanded the land effort at El Alamein and in Normandy. In the Soviet Union Stalin chaired the State Defence Committee from July 1941, Timoshenko directed the defence against Barbarossa, and from 1942 Zhukov headed the Stavka, directing the counter-stroke at Stalingrad, Kursk and the drive on Berlin, with Rokossovsky and Vatutin commanding the Leningrad and Kalinin fronts respectively. In China Chiang Kai-shek was supreme commander, Li Zongren commanded the defence of Taierzhuang, Xue Yue the third battle of Changsha, Zhang Zizhong was killed in action in May 1940, and Peng Dehuai opened the Hundred Regiments Offensive in August 1940. Technology and intelligence mattered as much: Robert Watson-Watt proposed pulse radar for aircraft detection in 1935 and the Tizard Mission carried the work to the United States; the Bletchley Park team under Alan Turing read German traffic, with the results directly shaping Allied deployment before Overlord; American naval cryptography broke the Japanese fleet code and produced the opening attack at Midway.
kits: 卡面那門一八五〇年的德國嘴射野戰砲，是普魯士克虜伯同年首次鑄成鋼製後膛那一代技術的產物。線膛配合銅殼或鋼芯炮彈，讓同樣藥量走得更遠；鋼製後膛抵住線膛帶來的高壓，前膛可以整門退回掩體後裝填，砲兵第一次能在射程上贏步兵。德國陸軍正由這條線起步：一八五〇年代換裝線膛野戰砲，一八七〇年代液壓後坐裝置成熟，數十名砲手不必再跑向前膛開門，一門砲的射速由每分鐘數發提高到十幾發，砲組可以全部蹲在砲後操作。到一九三九年，德軍野戰砲已全部是後膛式：步兵師屬裝七七公分輕型野戰砲，軍屬裝十點五公分輕野戰榴彈砲與十五公分重野戰榴彈砲，另有十五厘分配制退彈器的重砲，營連級別配三七公分反戰車砲。真正決定節奏的是量產：德國一九四四年產出約一萬九千輛戰車與自行火砲，其中四二式戰車逾六千輛；美軍一九四三年造出一百零三萬輛戰車與自行火砲、一千八百三十五萬輛卡車、逾八萬五千架飛機；蘇聯一九四三年造出一萬四千六百輛戰車與自行火砲、三萬四千九百架飛機。德國七七公分高射炮同時是反戰車主力，擊毀蘇聯T-34數百輛；蘇聯以四十五毫米一三七式、五十七毫米ZiS-3與七六毫米ZiS-2反戰車砲應戰，盟軍用六磅砲與二點八公分火箭筒。步兵方面，德軍主力是一九三五年式毛瑟步槍與突擊步槍，英美為李-恩菲爾德與M1加蘭特，蘇聯為莫辛-納甘與PPSh-41，日軍為三八式有坂。汽車與馬匹同時並行：德軍靠三噸半六乘四卡車與馱馬車隊維持補給，蘇軍在東線大量使用人推挽具與單馬挽車，美軍在遠東戰線直到一九四五年仍靠數十萬匹軍馬馱運。艦砲方面，德國俾斯麥號的三十八公分主砲與日本大和級的四十六公分主砲，是這條技術線的最後一級頂點。
kitsEn: The muzzle-loading field gun on the card, a German weapon of 1850, belongs to the generation that produced Krupp's first successful cast steel breech block in that same year. Rifling combined with copper or steel-cored shot let the same charge of powder reach further, and the steel breech withstood the pressures rifling brought with it, so a gun could be withdrawn intact behind cover for loading; artillery could for the first time outrange infantry. The German army set out along exactly that road: rifled field guns in the 1850s, and by the 1870s the hydraulic recoil apparatus had matured so that dozens of men no longer had to run forward to the muzzle to swab the bore, a single gun went from a few rounds a minute to well over ten, and the whole crew could work crouched behind the piece. By 1939 every German field gun was breech-loading: the 7.7 cm leichte Feldgeschütz in infantry divisions, the 10.5 cm leichte Feldhaubitze and 15 cm schwere Feldhaubitze at corps level, a 15 cm heavy gun with muzzle brake, and 3.7 cm anti-tank guns at battalion and company level. What really set the pace was mass production: Germany built about 19,000 tanks and self-propelled guns in 1944, of which more than 6,000 were Panzer IVs; the United States produced 1,034,100 tanks and self-propelled guns, 18,350,000 trucks and more than 85,000 aircraft in 1943; the Soviet Union turned out 14,600 tanks and self-propelled guns and 34,900 aircraft in 1943. The German 8.8 cm Flak served simultaneously as the main anti-tank weapon, destroying several hundred Soviet T-34s; the Soviets answered with the 45 mm Model 1937, the 57 mm ZiS-3 and the 76 mm ZiS-2, while the Allies used the 6-pounder and the 2.8 cm rocket launcher. On foot, the Wehrmacht relied on the Model 1898 Mauser and the assault rifle Gewehr 43, Britain and America on the Lee-Enfield and the M1 Garand, the Soviet Union on the Mosin-Nagant and PPSh-41, Japan on the Type 38 Arisaka. Motor vehicles and horses ran in parallel: the Germans moved supplies on three-and-a-half ton six-by-four trucks and horse-drawn wagons, the Soviets in the east made heavy use of man-pulled carts and single-horse carts, and American forces in the Pacific theatre were still relying on several hundred thousand army horses until 1945. In naval guns, the 38 cm main battery of the Bismarck and the 46 cm guns of the Yamato class marked the last full measure of that line.
tactics:
德軍在波蘭、法國與巴巴羅莎開出的打法，學術上稱為閃電戰，實質是空地協同的合成戰：Ju 87俯衝轟炸機與中型轟炸機先以低空掃射與炸彈打散前線，砲兵群隨即以曲射火力覆蓋縱深，戰車旅緊接著以每日數十公里的速度鑽進突破口，摩托化步兵搭乘半履帶車跟在後面佔領殘餘陣地，工兵在戰車身後迅速架設渡河器材。進攻重點集中於一點，裝甲集群在突破處形成數倍於步兵的火力密度，裝甲師與步兵師之間靠無線電與摩托車傳令保持聯繫，巴巴羅莎前線一度推到莫斯科城下，戰車集團衝鋒一日可行數十公里。
蘇聯在1942年後發展出縱深戰：以步兵加戰車的縱隊連續突破打擊德軍縱深，砲兵群由最高射界向前移動，集團軍與方面軍作戰在戰術階段結合火箭砲與空軍近距支援，1943年庫爾斯克前一次縱深突擊前佈置了上萬門砲與迫擊砲，一日發射約一百萬發炮彈。守方戰術同樣成型：法國馬奇諾防線以永久性砲壘、機槍巢與反砲兵群組成，重砲射界互相交叉；蘇聯的戰時國土在1941年後大量挖掘反戰車壕、佈設雷場、修築土木砲壘；德國在東線實行少量最新式重型戰車在後方集中、一發現即呼叫俯衝轟炸機與近距砲兵的戰術。海上是潛艇狼群與護航體系，港口以探照燈與深水炸彈反潛；登陸作戰以兩棲艦艇、艦砲射擊與空降部隊配合，1944年諾曼第的桑樹人工港與空降師在第一週就建立灘頭後勤。戰略轟炸分成兩條路：英國皇家空軍夜間對城市進行面積轟炸，美國陸軍航空隊以日間精確轟炸打擊合成燃料與交通目標。
tacticsEn:
The German method in Poland, in France and in Operation Barbarossa is usually called blitzkrieg, and in practice it was combined-arms war with close air support. Ju 87 dive bombers and medium bombers first broke up the front line with strafing runs and bombs; the artillery groups followed immediately, saturating the depth with high-angle fire; the tank brigades then drove into the breach at tens of kilometres a day, motorised infantry followed in half-tracks to occupy the ground left behind, and engineer units bridged rivers ahead of the armour. The weight of the attack was concentrated on a single Schwerpunkt, where the armoured mass achieved several times the infantry's rate of fire, and panzer and infantry divisions stayed in contact by wireless and motorcycle despatch riders; on the Barbarossa front the spearheads reached the approaches to Moscow, with armoured formations advancing tens of kilometres in a day.
From 1942 the Soviet Union developed the deep operation, with infantry and tank columns breaking through repeatedly to strike the German rear, artillery groups displaced forward from their maximum range, and army and front operations linked at tactical level to rocket artillery and close air support; before the Soviet deep stroke at Kursk in 1943 more than ten thousand guns and mortars were emplaced and roughly a million shells were fired in a single day. Defensive tactics matured as well. The French Maginot Line was built from permanent artillery casemates, machine-gun nests and counter-battery groups with interlocking heavy gun arcs. Soviet territory after 1941 was covered with anti-tank ditches, minefields, field works and earthen emplacements. Germany on the eastern front concentrated a small number of the newest heavy tanks in the rear, and once they were identified called in dive bombers and close artillery. At sea the pattern was wolf packs against convoys, with harbour defences using searchlights and depth charges against submarines. Amphibious landings combined landing craft with naval gunfire and airborne troops; the Mulberry harbour and the airborne divisions at Normandy established beachhead logistics within the first week. Strategic bombing ran along two lines: the Royal Air Force bombing cities by night, and the United States Army Air Forces flying daylight precision missions against synthetic fuel and transport targets.
data: 一九三九年波蘭戰役，德軍投入約一百五十萬人、約二千七百五十輛戰車與約二千架作戰飛機；波軍約一百萬人、三十九個步兵師加預備隊，約八百八十輛輕型戰車與不足四百架飛機，戰役共三十六日，波軍主力於十月六日被合圍殲滅。一九四〇年敦刻爾克，五月二十六日至六月四日共撤出三十二萬八千餘人。一九四一年巴巴羅莎，德軍以約三百萬人、三千五百輛戰車、數千架作戰飛機入侵，蘇軍初期可用兵力約二百九十萬、戰車近二千輛、飛機逾一萬架，戰役首月德軍推進約六百公里。一九四二年十一月蘇軍以約一百一十萬人、逾一千四百輛戰車、五百架飛機包圍德軍第六集團軍，被圍部隊約二十六萬人，最終突圍與投降者合計不足十萬。一九四三年七月庫爾斯克，德蘇各投入約七十八萬與一百九十萬人，參戰戰車逾兩千輛。一九四二年十至十一月阿拉曼，英軍約十九萬五千人對軸心國十一萬六千人，軸心國損失約三萬人。一九四四年六月六日，盟軍當日在五個海灘登陸約十五萬六千人，總損失約一萬人，至九月底諾曼第共登陸約二百萬人。一九四四年十二月至一九四五年的阿登突出部，德軍投入約六十一萬人，盟軍應戰兵力約六十一萬人。一九四五年四月柏林攻勢，蘇軍投入約二百五十萬人、四萬一千門砲、六千二百五十輛戰車、七千五百架飛機。產量方面，德國整場戰爭產出約十一萬九千架飛機，蘇聯約十五萬七千架，美國約三十二萬架，英國約十三萬一千架；戰車與自行火砲蘇聯約十萬五千輛，美國約八萬八千輛，德國約四萬六千輛。損失方面，德國軍人陣亡約五百三十萬，蘇聯軍人陣亡約八百七十萬至一千零七十萬，中國軍人陣亡約三百萬至四百萬，日本軍人陣亡約二百一十萬至二百三十萬，美國軍方作戰死亡逾四十萬人，英國逾三十八萬人。
dataEn: In the Polish campaign of 1939 Germany committed about 1.5 million men, roughly 2,750 tanks and some 2,000 combat aircraft; Poland fielded about a million men, thirty-nine infantry divisions plus reserves, some 880 light tanks and fewer than 400 aircraft, and the campaign ran for thirty-six days until the Polish field army was encircled and destroyed on 6 October. At Dunkirk, from 26 May to 4 June 1940, some 338,000 men were evacuated. In Operation Barbarossa the Germans invaded with about three million men, 3,500 tanks and several thousand combat aircraft, against roughly 2.9 million available Soviet troops, close to 2,000 tanks and more than 10,000 aircraft; German advance in the first month of the campaign was about 600 kilometres. In November 1942 the Soviet counter-offensive, Uranus, encircled the German Sixth Army with about 1.1 million troops, over 1,400 tanks and 500 aircraft against a pocket of roughly 260,000 German soldiers, of whom fewer than 100,000 eventually broke out or surrendered. At Kursk in July 1943 the two sides committed about 780,000 and 1.9 million men with more than 2,000 tanks engaged. At El Alamein in October and November 1942 the British fielded about 195,000 men against 116,000 Axis troops, and the Axis lost roughly 30,000. On 6 June 1944 the Allies landed about 156,000 men on five beaches at a total cost of some 10,000 casualties, and by the end of September around two million had landed in Normandy. In the Ardennes offensive from December 1944 to January 1945 Germany committed about 610,000 men against a similarly sized Allied force. For the assault on Berlin in April 1945 the Soviets brought about 2.5 million men, 41,000 guns, 6,250 tanks and 7,500 aircraft. On output, Germany built some 119,000 aircraft over the war, the Soviet Union about 157,000, the United States about 320,000 and Britain about 131,000; in tanks and self-propelled guns the Soviet Union produced some 105,000, the United States about 88,000 and Germany about 46,000. In losses, roughly 5.3 million German servicemen were killed, Soviet military dead number between about 8.7 and 10.7 million, Chinese military dead between 3 and 4 million, Japanese military dead between about 2.1 and 2.3 million, while more than 400,000 American and over 380,000 British military personnel died.
cause:
起因可分遠因、導火線與各戰線自身算計三層。遠因是一九一九年凡爾賽和約留下的種族、國界與軍備三重羞辱；德國在一九二〇年代暗中保留龐大軍火工業，一九三五年撕毀凡爾賽限制，一九三六年進駐萊茵蘭非軍事區，一九三八年吞併奧地利、肢解捷克斯洛伐克，一九三九年三月佔領布拉格。國際體系失效是另一層原因：國際聯盟在滿洲事變與義大利入侵衣索比中無力制裁，英法在慕尼黑會議上把蘇台德地區讓給德國，法國的財政與國防混亂使支援停留在口頭，美國的中立主義讓主要保障者缺席，德國則在西班牙內戰中以「民族社會主義」名義暗助叛軍，兩大陣營先在代理戰爭中互相消耗。
導火線是一九三九年八月二十三日德蘇互不侵犯條約，它為德軍騰出兩面受敵的顧慮；九月一日清晨德軍越過波蘭邊界，飛炸機在維利烏尼上空投下第一批炸彈，波蘭當日宣戰，英法於九月三日宣戰，北大西洋的海權國家就此被拖入戰爭。軸心國內部各有各的時鐘：日本在一九三一年佔領滿洲、一九三七年全面侵華，在南進資源爭奪與西方制裁之間走向一九四一年十二月七日的偷襲珍珠港；墨索里尼在法國崩潰後被連勝刺激，一九四〇年六月對英法宣戰，一九四一年十二月再對美國宣戰。亞洲方面，中國自一九三七年起獨力抵抗日本超過四年，消耗了日本大量陸軍兵力，這是日本必須向南方和太平洋擴張、奪取石油與原料的直接原因。
causeEn:
The origins fall into three layers: long-term causes, the immediate trigger, and the separate calculations of each theatre. The long-term cause was the triple humiliation of race, borders and armaments left by the Treaty of Versailles of 1919. Germany secretly kept a large war industry alive through the 1920s, tore up the Versailles limits in 1935, moved into the Rhineland's demilitarised zone in 1936, annexed Austria and dismembered Czechoslovakia in 1938, and occupied Prague in March 1939. The failure of the international system was a second layer. The League of Nations could not sanction Japan over Manchuria or Italy over Ethiopia; Britain and France handed the Sudetenland to Germany at Munich; French finances and military disorder kept its support at the level of words; American neutrality removed the principal guarantor of the Versailles settlement; and Germany supported the rebels in the Spanish Civil War under the banner of national socialism, so that the two future blocs wore each other down in a proxy war first.
The trigger was the German-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact of 23 August 1939, which relieved Germany of the fear of a two-front war. Early on 1 September German forces crossed the Polish border and aircraft dropped the first bombs over Wieluń; Poland declared war that day, Britain and France on 3 September, and the maritime powers of the Atlantic were drawn into the conflict. Within the Axis each member ran on its own clock. Japan had taken Manchuria in 1931 and fought a full-scale war in China from 1937, and moved between the pull of southern resources and Western sanctions towards the attack on Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941. Mussolini in Italy, spurred on by the collapse of France, declared war on Britain and France in June 1940 and on the United States in December 1941. In Asia, China had been resisting Japan alone for more than four years from 1937, consuming a large part of the Japanese army, and that was the direct reason Japan had to expand southward and into the Pacific to seize oil and raw materials.
impact:
這場戰爭的結果並非某一條戰線的勝負，而是把世界政治的重心整體挪了一次位置。歐洲由戰前列強主導的舊秩序，變成美國與蘇聯兩個戰時盟國分別佔據西歐與東歐的超級大國格局：一九四五年雅爾塔與波茨坦會議劃定中歐邊界，德國被分區佔領並最終分裂，波蘭整體西移，東歐三國被蘇聯吞併，聯合國於同年十月成立。戰後西歐與日本在美國援助下重建，馬歇爾計畫於一九四八年啟動，日本則放棄戰時擴張並在美國框架下重新武裝，長期走向工業復甦。舊殖民體系同時瓦解，亞非許多國家在戰後的民族主義浪潮中取得獨立，聯合國憲章把民族自決寫成條文。
在軍事技術上，這場戰爭確立了合成戰、縱深作戰與工業總動員三條主線，也把砲兵從配屬於步兵的支援武器徹底改造成量產的工業品。卡面那門一八五〇年的嘴射野戰砲所確立的線膛加鋼製後膛路線，到一九三九年已是全世界陸軍的共同標準，砲兵不再是配角，而是決定攻防節奏與兵力分配的樞紐。與此同時，總動員的邏輯把國家財政、交通、勞動與後方動員全部拉進戰爭，戰俘制度的現代化、紐倫堡審判、一九四九年日內瓦公約與國際人道法都進入新階段。最沉重的變化是核武：廣島與長崎之後，武器的破壞上限被一次性推高，此後的戰爭策劃從殲滅對方軍隊轉向避免被對方殲滅的恐怖平衡，一九四六年杜魯門提出遏制戰略，冷戰的基本架構由此形成。
impactEn:
The outcome of this war was not the balance of any single front but a wholesale shift in the centre of world politics. Europe moved from the old order led by the pre-war powers into a bipolar arrangement in which the two wartime allies, the United States and the Soviet Union, held the west and the east of the continent respectively. The Yalta and Potsdam conferences of 1945 drew the boundaries of central Europe; Germany was occupied in zones and eventually divided; Poland was moved bodily westward; the three Baltic states were absorbed by the Soviet Union; and the United Nations was founded that October. Western Europe and Japan rebuilt under American aid, with the Marshall Plan starting in 1948, while Japan abandoned its wartime expansion, rearmed inside the American framework and moved towards industrial recovery over the long run. The old colonial order broke down at the same time; many countries in Asia and Africa won independence in the post-war tide of nationalism, and the United Nations Charter put the principle of self-determination into articles.
In military terms the war settled three main lines: combined-arms operations, deep battle and industrial mobilisation. It also turned artillery from a support arm attached to infantry into a mass-produced industrial product. The line established by the muzzle-loading field gun on the card, rifling plus a steel breech, was by 1939 the common standard of every army in the world, and artillery was no longer a secondary arm but the pivot that set the rhythm of attack and defence and the distribution of force. The logic of total mobilisation likewise pulled state finance, transport, labour and the home front into the war, while the modernisation of the prisoner's regime, the Nuremberg trials, the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and international humanitarian law all entered a new phase. The gravest change was nuclear weapons: after Hiroshima and Nagasaki the ceiling of destruction was lifted in a single step, and war planning shifted from destroying the enemy's army towards a balance of terror that avoided being destroyed. Truman's containment strategy of 1946 grew out of that, and the basic architecture of the Cold War dates from it.
result:
結果分三段收場。義大利在北非、西西里與薩伏納等地接連失利後，墨索里尼於一九四三年七月被免職，意大利政府九月三日與盟國簽署停戰協定，十月十三日對德宣戰，德軍隨後逐步撤出意大利北部，一九四四年六月盟軍進入羅馬，戰線於一九四五年四月二十五日以德軍在意大利北部全面投降告終。歐洲方面，德國在東西兩面夾擊下崩潰：一九四五年初蘇軍自波羅的海與奧得河推進，先後攻下華沙、克拉科夫與維斯瓦河下游，進入柏林前在奧得河畔的澤勞弗沼澤地打成慘烈橋頭堡戰；四月十六日蘇軍以約二百五十萬人發動總攻，四月三十日蘇軍在國會大廈插旗，五月二日守軍投降，德軍參謀總長約德爾在投降書上簽名；五月七日艾森豪威爾在雷姆宣布停戰，五月八日午夜德國在三國佔領區首府廣播投降，歐洲戰事全面結束。
太平洋方面，日本在原子彈、蘇聯參戰與盟軍持續攻擊三重壓力下，裕仁天皇於一九四五年八月十五日以詔書宣布接受波茨坦宣言；九月二日代表日本在停泊於東京灣的密蘇里號戰艦上簽署投降書，第二次世界大戰以六年的全球戰事正式落幕；中國戰場受降儀式於九月九日在南京舉行，接收與復員隨即展開。戰後清算漫長：德國被分區佔領並劃定國界，日本被盟軍主要由美國佔領、解除武裝並在東京遠東軍事法庭受審，軸心國喪失大量領土與軍備，德國在歐洲的擴張被徹底逆轉，歐洲與亞洲的殖民秩序再未恢復舊貌。六十餘國留下的軍力與戰爭教訓，此後數十年成為各國國防建設的參照，而總體戰這個概念本身則成為冷戰初期各國規劃國防的共同語言。
resultEn:
The war closed in three stages. Italy lost North Africa, Sicily and the Salerno landings in turn; Mussolini was dismissed in July 1943, the Italian government signed an armistice with the Allies on 3 September and declared war on Germany on 13 October, German forces then withdrew by stages from northern Italy, the Allies entered Rome in June 1944, and the front in Italy ended with the German capitulation in the north on 25 April 1945. In Europe Germany collapsed under pressure from both fronts. In early 1945 the Red Army advanced from the Baltic and along the Oder, taking Warsaw, Cracow and the lower Vistula in turn, and fought a bitter bridgehead battle in the marshes around Seelow, east of the Oder, before entering Berlin. On 16 April the Soviets launched their general assault with about 2.5 million men, raised the flag on the Reichstag on 30 April, and the defenders capitulated on 2 May, with Generaloberst Jodl signing the surrender instrument. Eisenhower announced the armistice in Reims on 7 May, and at midnight on 8 May Germany broadcast its surrender from the capitals of the three occupation zones, ending the war in Europe.
In the Pacific, pressed on three sides at once by atomic bombs, the Soviet entry into the war and continued Allied attacks, the Emperor Hirohito announced by rescript on 15 August 1945 that Japan accepted the Potsdam Declaration. On 2 September representatives of Japan signed the instrument of surrender aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, formally closing six years of global war, and the Chinese surrender ceremony was held at Nanjing on 9 September, followed immediately by the takeover and demobilisation. The reckoning afterwards was long. Germany was occupied in zones and had its frontiers fixed; Japan was occupied, chiefly by the United States, disarmed and tried before the International Military Tribunal for the Far East; the Axis powers lost vast territories and armaments, Germany's attempt to dominate Europe was reversed for good, and the colonial order in Europe and Asia was never restored. The armed forces and the lessons left by more than sixty countries became the reference for defence planning in the decades that followed, and total war itself became the common language in which the new states of the early Cold War framed their security.
